states.label: Read the board after a forcing move
states.description: Look for a concrete theorem after the forcing move. If the opponent is checked, inspect every legal evasion and read the board again when we can move. Otherwise inspect checks and recaptures. If no theorem is visible on our turn, abandon this candidate; do not start another generic forcing search.

states.label: Check fork, collect, and protect
states.description: Check while attacking a loose piece. If every evasion preserves the fork, study a king escape that also defends another loose piece; otherwise inspect every evasion. Collect safely, taking a loose interposer with check first. Challenge the gain with safe checks, material-recovering captures, pawn or rook attacks, and queen attacks with additional king pressure; repair the threatened piece safely. This is selective continuation inspection, not a claim that all later replies are equivalent.

proof.scope: Selective human tactical policy. The check-fork card statically checks every immediate evasion for preservation of the attacked loose target, then examines constructive king escapes and declared counterattack classes. It does not assert dominance of that king escape or equivalence of all later counterplay. All other cards retain their prior complete check-evasion lists explicitly on the card.
proof.quiet_definition: No check, objective-erasing capture, immediate recapture, or safe nonpawn counterattack remains. Repaired-piece conclusions are stated separately on Secure the material gain.
